title: Code generation and metaprogramming
subtitle: I generate code where repetition is the risk: a generator that emits a whole function and wires it into the estate transactionally, and YAML tool schemas compiled into dispatch at build time.

lede: In FAFO Core and Function Forge, every new capability used to mean a person wiring a crate into the gateway, the control plane and the result path by hand, and a half-wired function shows up later as a hang. I decided agents should generate fully wired functions themselves, inside a sandbox, active only after a human rebuild. Function Forge is a Rust generator built on Handlebars templates and exposed as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool. One create function call emits the crate and, in the same rollback-protected transaction, edits the rest of the estate: the gateway's module, function and metadata definitions, the control plane's composition root and the completion service's dispatch.
evidence: Code generation and metaprogramming: a Rust generator on Handlebars templates that emits a crate of 8 + 6 files and edits four services in one rollback-protected transaction.
Tool synthesis and governed API integration: a vendor OpenAPI specification compiled into an internal catalog of 83 typed, costed operations, with about fifteen designed tools shown to agents.
Sandboxing for AI-authored code: generated logic confined to a developer zone with a capability-bounded context object, active only after a rebuild and a human restart.
Build-time schema compilation: YAML tool definitions compiled into dispatch code and JSON-Schema tool inputs at build time.
author: Corey James
